## Measurement spec

`spec:F4`

| field | value |
|---|---|
| collector | httpx |
| collector_pin | httpx>=0.27 |
| evidence_kind | changelog document + parse verdict |
| indicator_code | F4 |
| instrument_entry | assessment/instrument/RULE-F4-v5.yaml |
| instrument_state | project_defined |
| leg | F4 |
| mode | auto |
| prior_art | `usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide` |
| rf_ask_plain | The agency's change log or release notes, at each address on record. |
| rf_fail | For every data page looked at, no such feed was found at the recorded locations: there is no change history there, or there is one published as an ordinary web page, or its entries do not say what kind of change they are, or the recorded locations were missing or wrong. The project's format and labelling floors decide two of these, so a precise web-page change log that a machine can read, and that a Data on the Web Best Practice accepts, still fails here. A fail is not a claim that the version history is absent, incomplete or unreadable, nor that the agency does not publish revisions. |
| rf_fix_line | Publish a version history for the product. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can a machine learn what changed between releases? An SI client holding last month's figure needs to know it was revised, and why; without a change history it cannot tell a revision from an error. |
| rf_name_brief | A change history a program can follow |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not finish looking at one or more pages, for one of three reasons: the host turned the identified client away; the client's own honoring of the site's robots.txt stopped it reading the page; or a starting source was not searched, or a server or network error left the result unconfirmed. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages that were looked at met this and some did not. |
| rf_pass | Every data page that was looked at has a change history served as a JSON, Atom or RSS feed, with at least half its entries saying what kind of change they record. |
| rf_plain_name | Change history served as a structured feed |
| rf_question | Can a machine learn what changed between releases from a structured change history? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Provide a complete version history that explains the changes made in each version."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Check that a list of published versions is available as well as a change log describing precisely how each version differs from the previous one."}, {"source": "usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide", "quote": "Implement versioning so AI developers can track updates over time."}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_tells_plain | Whether software can see what changed between releases from a structured list of changes. |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client opens each recorded change-log location and reads what kind of document it sends and, for a feed, how many of its entries say what kind of change they record. |
| rf_where_we_look | Each change-log or release-notes location on record for the agency. |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A Data on the Web Best Practice asks for a complete version history that explains the changes in each version, and a published guide on data for developers asks for versioning so updates can be tracked over time. The added demands that the history come as a feed and that entries carry a change-type label are the project's own rules; neither source requires them. |
| rf_why_short | The World Wide Web Consortium asks publishers for a full version history; requiring it in a fixed structured form is this project's rule. |
| rule_id | RULE-F4-v5 |
| signal | Fetch any changelog or release-notes endpoint; test whether it is machine-readable and carries a revision class per entry. |
